data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C nuclear energy company that has raised $125M+ to date. The broader nuclear energy sector comp universe consists of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Antares.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($125M) as a baseline proxy and applying a typical Series C to next-stage multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $212M. A peer-median approach is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector; while four nuclear peers exist, none yielded sufficient datapoints across stage and valuation-tier filters to support a credible median calculation.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $181M (low) to $244M (high), with a median of $212M. This range is derived from a single methodology, which represents a material constraint on precision. Key uncertainties include the absence of robust same-stage private nuclear peers for cross-validation, the composition and stage distribution of the broader comp set, and whether the 1.7x multiplier appropriately reflects market conditions and Kyoto's specific risk profile relative to peer progression. Additional data on comparable Series C valuations in adjacent frontier energy or hard-tech sectors would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
